name: Hard Trance / Hard House
summary: The UK hard-trance/hard-house lineage that runs from Trade and Tidy Trax through Nukleuz to the 2025-26 revival: a hard, punchy 4/4 kick, an open hat firing on every offbeat 8th (the genre's defining drive), 16th closed hats kept low, and a clap on 2 and 4 that regularly explodes into a 16th roll. Percussion bounces (congas, rim, clave loops) rather than washing; breakdowns embrace long euphoric builds and drop-into-silence gaps that hard techno deliberately avoids.

sounds.kick: Hard, clean, clipped 4/4 kick (909-style base) tuned for club weight rather than distortion-first; the revival keeps it punchy with a touch more low-mid than the 90s original.
sounds.snare: Clap on 2 and 4 is the primary backbeat; layered clap+snare stacks and 16th clap rolls (Nukleuz-style call-and-response) mark the harder/revival lanes. A true snare is rare outside 2020s revival layering.
sounds.hats: Open hat on every offbeat 8th at high velocity is the signature drive; closed 16ths sit under 70% so they never compete; double-offbeat variants (hits on both the 'and' and the 'a') push extra energy.
sounds.percussion: Bouncing congas, rim shots and compressed clave/schranz-adjacent loops fill the space the hoover bassline leaves; cowbell ghosts hoover stabs in gallop-style patterns.
sounds.cymbals: One crash marks riser payoffs and section changes; ride is used sparingly as an alternate groove engine (loud/soft 8ths), not a wash.

machines: Roland TR-909 — kick, clap, ride, hats
Roland TR-727 / TR-505 — congas and claves for bouncing percussion loops
Simmons SDS — toms for gallop/cascade risers
Novation Drumstation / Quasimidi 309 — period-correct rave claps and 909-style kicks
Elektron Machinedrum / Korg Electribe ER-1 — synthesised percussion for the schranz-hybrid lane
Roland Alpha Juno-2 (hoover source, bass not drums) — the offbeat hoover the drums are built to frame
Sonic Academy Kick 2 — modern synthesised kick design
